{{nihongo|'''Maki Kawai'''|川合眞紀|Kawai Maki}} is a Japanese chemist who developed spatially selective single-molecule spectroscopy. In 2018, she became the first woman to become president of the [[Chemical Society of Japan]].

==Early life and education==
Kawai earned her bachelor's degree at the [[University of Tokyo]] in 1975.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.k.u-tokyo.ac.jp/pros-e/person/maki_kawai/maki_kawai.htm|title=Maki Kawai|website=www.k.u-tokyo.ac.jp|language=en|access-date=2018-08-25|archive-date=2017-06-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170618224019/http://www.k.u-tokyo.ac.jp/pros-e/person/maki_kawai/maki_kawai.htm|url-status=dead}}</ref> She completed her doctoral studies at the [[University of Tokyo]] in 1980.<ref name=":0" /> Her PhD was supervised by Kenji Tamaru.

==Research and career==
[[File:Maki Kawai, Sam Aronson, and others, at 2012 signing of RIKEN-BNL agreement renewal.jpg|thumb|left|With [[Sam Aronson]] (Signing Ceremony for the agreement between [[Brookhaven National Laboratory]] and [[Riken]], 2012)]]
Kawai was a postdoctoral researcher at [[Riken]] between 1980 and 1982.<ref name=":1">{{Cite news|url=http://www.chemistry.or.jp/en/news/2017/prof-maki-kawai-is-elected-the-next-president-of-the-csj.html|title=Prof. Maki Kawai is elected the next President of the CSJ|work=The Chemical Society of Japan|access-date=2018-08-25|language=en-US}}</ref> She joined the [[University of Tokyo]] as a [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]] fellow in 1982.<ref name=":1" /> Her research considers the vibrational dynamics of single-molecules at surfaces.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://groups.oist.jp/ndu/event/single-molecule-spectroscopy-using-stm-prof-maki-kawai|title="Single molecule spectroscopy using STM" Prof. Maki Kawai {{!}} OIST Groups|website=groups.oist.jp|date=12 May 2015 |access-date=2018-08-25}}</ref><ref>{{Citation|last=KyushuUniv|title=2017/01/24 I²CNER Seminar Series Dr. Maki Kawai|date=2017-03-21|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_Q2KX0nUE5U|access-date=2018-08-25}}</ref><ref name="Katano 3003–3007">{{Cite journal|last1=Katano|first1=Satoshi|last2=Kim|first2=Yousoo|last3=Kagata|first3=Yuma|last4=Kawai|first4=Maki|date=2010-02-02|title=Single-Molecule Vibrational Spectroscopy and Inelastic-Tunneling-Electron-Induced Diffusion of Formate Adsorbed on Ni(110)|journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry C|language=EN|volume=114|issue=7|pages=3003–3007|doi=10.1021/jp909394q|issn=1932-7447}}</ref> Her group use STM to monitor molecules and atoms on top of surfaces.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.riken.jp/en/research/rikenresearch/highlights/5112/|title=Chemical reaction singled out {{!}} RIKEN|website=www.riken.jp|language=en|access-date=2018-08-25}}</ref> She uses this to understand the chemical and physical phenomena of nanowires, nanodots and biomolecules.<ref name=":0" /> She was awarded fellowships from the ''Surface Science Society of Japan'' and [[American Physical Society]] to develop single molecule spectroscopy.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|url=https://www.ims.ac.jp/en/research/head/kawai.html|title=KAWAI, Maki {{!}} Research {{!}} Institute for Molecular Science|website=www.ims.ac.jp|access-date=2018-08-25|archive-date=2018-08-26|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180826043954/https://www.ims.ac.jp/en/research/head/kawai.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Her group monitor the vibrational and relaxation energies of single molecules using [[Scanning tunneling microscope|scanning tunneling microscopy]] and inelastically tunnelled electrons.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.csj.jp/csj-en/membership/awards/achieve/2008-kawai.html|title=CSJ Award 2008-Prof.Maki Kawai|website=www.csj.jp|access-date=2018-08-25}}</ref> She has contributed to several books and hundreds of peer-reviewed publications.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=1juFUF9u2LIC&q=single+molecule+maki+kawai|title=Functionalization of Semiconductor Surfaces|last=Tao|first=Franklin (Feng)|date=2012-04-10|publisher=John Wiley & Sons|isbn=9780470562949|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hhsGCAAAQBAJ&q=maki+kawai&pg=PA215|title=Dynamic Processes on Solid Surfaces|last=Tamaru|first=Kenzi|date=2013-06-29|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9781489916365|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=7V2SK8ZIGBoC&q=maki+kawai&pg=PA271|title=One Hundred Years at the Intersection of Chemistry and Physics: The Fritz Haber Institute of the Max Planck Society 1911-2011|last1=James|first1=Jeremiah|last2=Steinhauser|first2=Thomas|last3=Hoffmann|first3=Dieter|last4=Friedrich|first4=Bretislav|date=2011-10-27|publisher=Walter de Gruyter|isbn=9783110239546|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.co.jp/citations?hl=ja&user=6_CXetMAAAAJ&view_op=list_works&sortby=pubdate|title=Maki Kawai - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.co.jp|access-date=2018-08-25}}</ref> Kawai continued to be supported by the [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]], investigating nanoscale electron transport through molecular layers.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.jsps.go.jp/j-grantsinaid/27_kdata/kohyo/data/h17/02/1-6-8.pdf|title=Grants in Aid|website=JSPS|access-date=2018-08-27}}</ref> By combining single molecule spectroscopy (using [[scanning tunneling spectroscopy]]) with [[inelastic electron tunneling spectroscopy]] to identify electron transfer channels.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://groups.oist.jp/ndu/event/single-molecule-spectroscopy-using-stm-prof-maki-kawai|title="Single molecule spectroscopy using STM" Prof. Maki Kawai {{!}} OIST Groups|website=groups.oist.jp|date=12 May 2015 |access-date=2018-08-27}}</ref><ref name="Katano 3003–3007"/> She discovered a new reaction pathway on the surface of [[titanium dioxide]].<ref>{{Cite news|title=New reaction pathway discovered|language=en|url=https://www.materialstoday.com/materials-chemistry/news/new-reaction-pathway-discovered/|access-date=2018-08-27}}{{Dead link|date=August 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Tunneling out of the surface|url=http://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2015-07/tu-too070915.php|access-date=2021-04-27|website=EurekAlert!|language=en|archive-date=2018-11-18|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181118183411/https://www.eurekalert.org/pub_releases/2015-07/tu-too070915.php|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|title=Tunneling out of the Surface|url=https://www.tohoku.ac.jp/en/press/news20150709.html|access-date=2021-04-27|website=www.tohoku.ac.jp|language=en}}</ref>

Kawai became Chief Scientist and Director of Surface Chemistry Laboratory at [[Riken]] in 1991 and an executive director in 2010.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.riken.go.jp/lab-www/surf-chem/maki/maki.html|title=Home page of Maki Kawai|website=www.riken.go.jp|access-date=2018-08-25|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170714200439/http://www.riken.go.jp/lab-www/surf-chem/maki/maki.html|archive-date=2017-07-14|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was made a professor at the [[University of Tokyo]] in 2004.<ref name=":1" /> Kawai joined the Institute of Molecular Science as Director General in 2016.<ref name=":1" /> She was appointed President of the [[Chemical Society of Japan]] in 2018.<ref name=":1" /><ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/japanese-chemical-society-elects-first-female-president/3009063.article|title=Japanese chemical society elects first female president|work=Chemistry World|access-date=2018-08-25|language=en}}</ref>
